pages.text: The $(item)Radio Cloner$() copies one radio's programming into others, as a radio shop's cloning cable does. Empty, use it on a radio to $(thing)read$() it; loaded, use it on as many radios as you like to $(thing)write$(). Sneak and use it in the air to clear it; sneak-use on a radio reads that one instead.$(br2)Use it on a placed radio, or in the air with a handheld in your other hand.

pages.title: What it copies
pages.text: $(li)$(l:radiocraft:radios/commercial_radios)Commercial radios$(): channels and contact list, into other commercial radios that can take them (a smaller radio takes what fits; the brick refuses digital). Each keeps its own unit ID. Keys marked not readable are $(thing)left behind$(): those channels arrive clear.$(li)2m ham radios: the dial (frequency, tones, offset) and a handheld's memory channels. Base stations have no memories.$(li)Marine radios have fixed channels: nothing to clone.
The cable on a box with its memory and logic.
